name: Build and update the project schedule
summary: Every project has a critical path schedule that shows how the work will finish within the contract time. A scheduler builds the baseline from the contract and the superintendent's sequence, and then every month the field engineer records progress, the superintendent confirms it, the scheduler updates and analyses the schedule, and the project manager reviews it and sends it to the owner. When a milestone slips the team works out recovery and, if the owner caused it, gives notice of delay. It is slow because a dozen schedulers serve about 220 projects, and error-prone because progress is estimated by eye and field sequence changes are not always passed on.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 employees with about 220 active projects and a central scheduling group in operations support.
baseline.notes: Primavera P6 on large and P3 projects, Microsoft Project on smaller ones; progress collected on paper printouts or PDFs; updates shared as PDF Gantt charts.

trigger: The month-end data date passes on an active project (about 95% of cases), or the startup package for a new project arrives and a baseline is needed (about 5%).
end_state: The consultant accepts the monthly update or the baseline, and the three-week look-ahead is with the trades.

volume.seasonality: One update per active project each month; slightly more active projects from May to November.

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver active-projects (190-220-260) with one update each, plus about 10 baselines a month from project starts.

roles.title: Scheduler (CPM)
roles.department: Operations support (project controls, scheduling, VDC, quality)

systems.name: CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)

steps.name: Open the schedule case
steps.description: The scheduler assigned to the project opens the schedule file for the month: either a new project's startup package arrives and a baseline must be built, or the month-end data date has passed and the monthly update is due. He checks the folder, the last issued version and the owner's due date.
inputs: startup package or month-end data date

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: About 10 baselines a month (project starts) among about 220 monthly schedule cases, from the organisation file drivers.

steps.name: Review the contract time, milestones and estimate
steps.description: The scheduler reads the contract time, interim milestones, phasing and liquidated damages clauses, the estimate's duration assumptions and the site logistics plan, and agrees the work breakdown structure with the project manager.

error.defect_description: An interim milestone or phasing constraint is missed.

evidence.note: The construction schedule must show the work will be performed within the Contract Time (GC 3.4.1).

steps.name: Superintendent sets sequence and durations
steps.description: The superintendent marks up a sequence for the job: excavation and foundations, structure by floor or zone, envelope, rough-ins, finishes and commissioning, with crew-based durations and the long-lead deliveries he depends on.

error.defect_description: Durations copied from a past job without adjusting for this building's size or season.

evidence.note: Common CPM scheduling practice on Canadian building projects; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the CPM network
steps.description: The scheduler enters activities, durations and logic links in Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project, typically several hundred to over a thousand activities, adds procurement and submittal activities, owner milestones and a winter calendar, and runs the schedule to find the critical path.

error.defect_description: Open-ended activities or hard constraints that hide the true critical path.

evidence.note: Critical events and their relationships (GC 3.4.1); activities, milestones and contract time shown.

steps.name: Review the draft baseline with the project team
steps.description: The project manager runs a review session with the superintendent and scheduler, walks the critical path and float, tests the sequence against the buyout plan and logistics, and lists changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common CPM scheduling practice on Canadian building projects; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Finalise the baseline
steps.description: The scheduler makes the agreed changes or the consultant's revisions, checks logic quality (open ends, constraints, lags), assigns cost or manpower loading where the contract asks for it, and prints the baseline Gantt chart and narrative.

error.defect_description: Version saved over the baseline copy.

evidence.note: Common CPM scheduling practice on Canadian building projects; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve and submit the baseline
steps.description: The project manager approves the baseline and submits it to the consultant and owner with a narrative, before the first application for payment as the contract requires.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 GC 3.4.1.1: construction schedule submitted before the first application for payment (contract requirement)

steps.name: Consultant and owner review the baseline
steps.description: The consultant and owner review the baseline for completeness, milestones and contract time and either accept it or return comments for revision.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Owner returns or requires revisions within 10 days in the Alberta specification; the 30% revision share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record progress on site
steps.description: The field engineer walks the site with the current three-week look-ahead and records actual start and finish dates and percent complete for each activity in progress, noting areas not started, trades short of manpower and work lost to weather.

error.defect_description: Percent complete overstated for an activity that is visibly started but far from done.

evidence.note: Updates reflect activity changes, completions and activities in progress.

steps.name: Superintendent confirms progress and remaining durations
steps.description: The superintendent checks the field engineer's mark-up, corrects percent complete, sets remaining durations and notes sequence changes he has already made in the field or plans for next month.

error.defect_description: A field sequence change is not passed on to the scheduler.

next.condition: larger project with a scheduler assigned
smaller project scheduled by the project team

evidence.note: Share of projects with a dedicated scheduler is the author's estimate: about 12 schedulers cannot update all 220 schedules, so smaller jobs keep a Microsoft Project schedule in the project team.

steps.name: Enter actuals and recalculate the schedule
steps.description: The scheduler keys actual dates, percent complete and remaining durations into the schedule, adjusts logic for the sequence changes, moves the data date to month end and recalculates.

error.defect_description: Actual date keyed to the wrong activity or out-of-sequence progress left unresolved.

evidence.note: Updated schedule due within 5 days after month end; schedulers carry several projects, causing the queue.

steps.name: Compare with baseline and analyse slippage
steps.description: The scheduler compares the update with the baseline and last month: critical path changes, float lost, milestones moved, and which activities drove the movement. He writes the variance section of the narrative.

error.defect_description: Driving cause attributed to the wrong activity.

next.condition: a milestone or completion date slips

evidence.note: Narrative compares progress to baseline and identifies problem areas and anticipated delays; slip share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Work out recovery options
steps.description: The superintendent and scheduler test ways to win back time: re-sequencing zones, adding a crew or shift, overtime, earlier deliveries or splitting activities, and estimate what each costs.

error.defect_description: Recovery plan relies on a crew that is not available.

evidence.note: Measures to regain slippage discussed for activities behind baseline.

steps.name: Decide cause and entitlement
steps.description: The project manager decides whether the delay was caused by the owner or consultant (changes, late RFI answers, late permits, unforeseen conditions), by weather, or by the company and its subcontractors, and whether to give notice of delay.

error.defect_description: Notice deadline missed because cause was unclear.

evidence.note: Share of slips that are owner-caused is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the delay notice and time impact analysis
steps.description: The project manager writes the notice of delay with the scheduler's time impact fragnet showing the delay inserted into the schedule, the affected milestones and the extension requested, and sends it to the consultant and the claims team.

error.defect_description: Fragnet not tied to the contemporaneous schedule, weakening the request.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 Part 6 (delays and extensions of Contract Time) and GC 3.4.1.3 schedule revisions

steps.name: Review the update before issue
steps.description: The project manager reads the updated schedule and narrative, checks that forecast dates match what he is telling the owner and that delays are described consistently with any notices, and approves it or sends corrections back.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common CPM scheduling practice on Canadian building projects; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Publish the update and three-week look-ahead
steps.description: The assistant project manager prints the updated Gantt chart, the narrative and a three-week look-ahead filtered by trade, and posts them to the project platform.

error.defect_description: Look-ahead filter drops a trade's activities.

steps.name: Issue the look-ahead to the trades
steps.description: The superintendent hands out and walks through the look-ahead at the weekly subcontractor coordination meeting, confirming each foreman's manpower and start dates for the next three weeks.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Schedule discussed at regular site meetings.

steps.name: Submit the update to the owner
steps.description: The project manager sends the updated schedule and narrative to the consultant and owner with the monthly progress report and draw, as the contract requires monthly.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 GC 3.4.1.2: schedule updated monthly or as the Contract Documents stipulate

steps.name: Consultant reviews the update
steps.description: The consultant reviews the update at or before the monthly owner meeting and accepts it or asks for revisions where progress or logic is questioned.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Review and revision cycle; acceptance share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the schedule in the project team
steps.description: On a smaller project the assistant project manager keys the confirmed progress and remaining durations into the Microsoft Project schedule, moves the status date, compares the forecast with the baseline milestones and notes any slippage for the project manager.

error.defect_description: Logic broken by typing actual dates over planned dates, hiding the real critical path.

next.condition: a milestone or completion date slips

evidence.note: Common CPM scheduling practice on Canadian building projects; durations are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Baseline for a new project
exceptions.description: A new project needs a baseline built, reviewed and accepted before the first draw.

exceptions.name: Critical slippage
exceptions.description: A milestone or completion date slips; recovery options are worked out and the cause decided.

exceptions.name: Owner-caused delay notice
exceptions.description: The delay is owner-caused and the project manager issues a delay notice with a time impact analysis.

exceptions.name: Update corrected before issue or after consultant comments
exceptions.description: The project manager or consultant questions progress or logic and the update is reworked.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end data date to accepted update (monthly cases)
benchmarks.population: Canadian building projects with monthly schedule updates

evidence.note: The Alberta specification requires the update within 5 days after month end and gives the owner 10 days to review; in practice submissions run a few days late. p50 and p90 are the author's reading.

benchmarks.unit: days after commencement for the initial schedule

pain_points.description: About a dozen schedulers support about 220 projects, so updates queue behind each other at month end.

evidence.note: Organisation file: 12 schedulers; workload derived from the step times.

pain_points.description: Progress is estimated by eye on paper printouts and re-keyed into the scheduling software, so percent complete is often optimistic.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice.

pain_points.description: Sequence changes made in the field reach the scheduler late, so the issued schedule does not match how the job is being built.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Delay notices are given late or without a contemporaneous schedule analysis, weakening extension of time requests.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: CCDC 2 - 2020 Stipulated Price Contract (standard form text in a District of Hudson's Hope tender package)
sources.publisher: Canadian Construction Documents Committee; document posted by the District of Hudson's Hope
sources.supports: GC 3.4.1: construction schedule submitted to owner and consultant before the first application for payment, showing major activities and critical events, monitored and updated monthly or as the Contract Documents state, consultant advised of revisions from extensions of Contract Time; GC 3.6.1: contractor makes written agreements with subcontractors and suppliers that incorporate the prime contract terms; GC 3.6.2-3.6.3: owner may object to a proposed subcontractor before signing; GC 5.2.4: schedule of values at least 15 calendar days before the first application for payment; GC 9.4.1: contractor establishes, maintains and supervises health and safety precautions and programs; GC 10.4.1: evidence of workers' compensation compliance before commencing the Work and with each application for payment; GC 11.1: contractor insurance per CCDC 41.

sources.title: Section 01321 Bar Chart Construction Schedule (standard specification)
sources.supports: Initial construction schedule within 15 days after commencement; owner returns it or requires revisions within 10 days of receipt; revised schedule within 5 days of comments; updated schedule within 5 days after the end of each month; progress revisions within 15 days of notice when progress departs from the schedule and substantial performance is in jeopardy.

sources.title: Section 01 32 16 Construction Progress Schedule (National Master Specification based section in City of Winnipeg Bid Opportunity 21-2017)
sources.supports: Schedule updates reflect activity changes, completions and activities in progress, with a narrative comparing progress to baseline, current forecasts, problem areas, anticipated delays and mitigation; the schedule is discussed at regular site meetings, with activities behind baseline identified and recovery measures given; weather delays discussed.

assumptions: One case is one project's schedule cycle in a month; about 4.5% of cases are new baselines (10 starts among about 220 cases). Baseline and update follow different paths in the same file.
The monthly cycle starts at the data date, not at the start of the month, so the cycle time measures turnaround of the update, not the reporting period.

Schedulers update about 55% of projects (larger and P3 jobs); on the rest the assistant project manager keeps a Microsoft Project schedule (s21). With every update on schedulers, the step times imply about 14 scheduler FTE against 12 in the organisation file. The org file's process roles omit assistant-pm and field-engineer, which are used here.
fte_on_process for each role = mean hands-on hours per case from the steps x 220 cases a month / 130 productive hours, plus 15% for coordination not written as steps.

The simulated median turnaround (about 13 days) is a little above the 11-day benchmark because the simulation adds the queue at each step in sequence; the Alberta 5-day submission target is rarely met on busy month ends.
The look-ahead to trades and the submission to the owner run in parallel and are listed in sequence with concurrent_with.

Produces adds private-owner and ops-progress-draw links that the org file's process map lacks; private owners also receive schedules, and the accepted baseline is a precondition of the first draw under CCDC 2 GC 3.4.1.
